maria.nguyen: FYI, after the kernel-selector change landed we saw a regression on a couple of long-seq jobs. ~18% lower throughput for seq=2048, interleaved KV, stride=128. posting perf dump here.
kai.singh: Ugh. Is that the selector that prefers fused-flash for small-batch low-latency? thought it had fallback for paged.
dave.lee: Right, the new rule picks fused-flash when estimated_bank_conflicts < 10. Looks like our bank-conflict estimator undercounts for interleaved layout.
maria.nguyen: Attached profiler snippet:
```
GPU: A100
seq_len=2048, batch=4
chosen_kernel: fused_flash_v2
measured_tokens/s: 1456
expected_tokens/s (old): 1760
SM utilization: 78% -> dropped
warp_stall_mem: +22%
bank_conflicts metric: 12 (estimator reported 3)
```
nina.patel: Can you paste the estimator code? I suspect we used stride/warp assumptions for separate layout.
oliver.cho: Estimator is in runtime/heuristics/kernel_select.cc: calc_conflict_score(interleave, stride)
kai.singh: Quick grep shows calc_conflict_score assumes 64-byte alignment and computes warps = stride/64 which breaks when dtype=bfloat16 (2 bytes) vs fp16 (2 bytes) vs int8 (1 byte) leading to wrong lanes per bank.
dave.lee: Ah —some of those jobs use bf16 packing and our allocator returns 256-byte aligned blocks so effective stride in lanes != assumed. estimator multiplies by element_size but we missed packed-kv case.
maria.nguyen: Repro steps I ran:
```
./tools/run_microbench --model=gpt2xl --seq=2048 --batch=4 --kv-layout=interleaved --dtype=bfloat16 --stride=128
perf dump > /tmp/dump.log
```
kai.singh: I ran microbench with int8 and didn't see regression. So dtype matters.
oliver.cho: Suggestion: change estimator to compute bank index via (addr / bank_size_bytes) % banks using actual pointer arithmetic from allocated base instead of stride heuristics.
nina.patel: Also, the selector's threshold (conflict < 10) is too aggressive. For seq>1024 fused_flash wins only if conflict < 3 in practice.
dave.lee: We should add an override that forces paged-flash for interleaved layouts with stride >= 128 and dtype in {bfloat16, fp16} until we fix estimator.
perf-bot: Automated note: canary job triggered for customer XYZ at 2026-03-18T09:12:01Z — 3% error budget remaining.
maria.nguyen: Plan: 1) quick canary rollback of kernel-selector change (config flag) 2) patch estimator to use allocation metadata + dtype 3) add unit test fuzzer across strides/dtypes 4) run 2x canary runs then promote.
oliver.cho: Also add metric "kernel_selector/estimator_mismatch" when measured_bank_conflicts > predicted*2 so we can alert.
kai.singh: I'll submit a small revert PR for the selector config flag now.
dave.lee: I'll prototype estimator fix. Nina can you own the canary runs and dashboards?
nina.patel: Yep, will set up a dashboard with tokens/s and bank_conflict_ratio and add alert at ratio>1.5.
maria.nguyen: One more: add an allocator alignment test that ensures KV base pointers are 64-byte aligned for fused kernels; currently packaging sometimes aligns to 256 and that changes conflict pattern.
oliver.cho: For the long term, we should support both interleaved and separate layouts in the estimator and make selector aware of memory allocator guarantees per deployment (hosted vs dedicated). different kernels assume different guarantees.
perf-bot: Benchmark snapshot uploaded: /perf/snapshots/2134567890/ — diff shows -17.5% tokens/s for fused_flash_v2 on interleaved+bfloat16
sre-bot: Incident note: no customer-facing degradation observed yet; throttling canary/releases if regression >10% across >=3 jobs.
kai.singh: Cool. I'll tag PRs: revert PR #4523, estimator fix PR #4524 (draft).
maria.nguyen: Thanks team. Nina, once canary green, let's coordinate a staged re-roll with the improved estimator and metric gating. :thumbsup:
